short: Edit distance into $\ell_1$: the sharp exponent

title.title: Edit distance into $\ell_1$: the exponent is right
title.subtitle: Claim: embedding edit distance on length-$d$ strings into $\ell_1$ needs distortion $\exp(\Theta(\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}))$

plain: How well can 'number of typing edits between two words' be mimicked by a simple sum of differences?

beats.text: Log of the best distortion, against $\log d$; constants schematic
For twenty years: Ostrovsky–Rabani above, only $\Omega(\log d)$ below
Claim: the lower bound has the same shape. The 2007 embedding is optimal

steps: Build words in levels, with parts cycling at different prime periods
At each level, sums of cuts lag behind edit distance
The lag compounds across levels, matching the known embedding

data.label: the lag compounds level by level

before.label: Best lower bound, 2009
before.note: Krauthgamer–Rabani; the upper bound was exponentially larger

after.label: Claimed, 27 Sep 2026
